questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Clarify supports SHAP-based explainability for NLP models, showing which tokens or words in the input text most influenced the model's prediction. For example, in a sentiment analysis model, SageMaker Clarify can highlight that the word 'excellent' contributed positively to a positive sentiment prediction. This extends beyond tabular data to support the growing use of NLP models in production.

questions.question: A government agency wants to use AI for benefit eligibility determinations. Under responsible AI principles, which requirement is MOST critical?

options.A: The system should process applications as fast as possible
options.B: The system must be explainable, fair, and include a robust appeals process with human review
options.C: The system should use the most complex model available for maximum accuracy
options.D: The system should be fully autonomous with no human intervention

questions.explanation: Government benefit eligibility determinations significantly affect people's lives and involve public accountability. The system must be explainable (so applicants understand decisions), fair (so no demographic group is systematically disadvantaged), and include a robust appeals process with human review (so incorrect or unfair decisions can be challenged and reversed). Many regulations also require these safeguards for government automated decision-making.

questions.question: What is 'concept drift' and how does it affect the fairness of a deployed model?

options.A: Concept drift refers to the model architecture changing over time; it has no effect on fairness
options.B: Concept drift occurs when the underlying relationship between features and the target changes; it can cause fairness degradation because the model's biases may shift in unpredictable ways as real-world conditions change
options.C: Concept drift is when the model's source code changes; it improves fairness automatically
options.D: Concept drift refers to changes in team understanding of AI concepts

questions.explanation: Concept drift occurs when the statistical relationship between input features and the target variable changes over time (e.g., what constitutes a 'good' loan applicant may change during an economic downturn). This can degrade fairness because the model was calibrated for a different set of relationships. Groups that were fairly treated under the original conditions may become unfairly treated as conditions shift, making continuous fairness monitoring essential.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of applying the 'safety' pillar of responsible AI?

options.A: Publishing the model's performance metrics
options.B: Implementing kill switches, fallback mechanisms, and guardrails that prevent the AI system from causing harm even when it produces unexpected outputs
options.C: Reducing model training costs
options.D: Using a larger training dataset

questions.explanation: The safety pillar of responsible AI focuses on preventing AI systems from causing harm. Practical implementations include kill switches (ability to quickly shut down the system), fallback mechanisms (graceful degradation to safer behavior when the AI encounters unexpected situations), output guardrails (filtering or constraining outputs to prevent harmful actions), and safe defaults (conservative behavior in uncertain situations). These measures ensure the system remains safe even when it encounters edge cases.

questions.question: What does AWS Config provide that supports AI governance?

options.A: Bias detection in ML models
options.B: Continuous tracking and recording of AWS resource configurations, enabling organizations to audit the state and changes of their AI/ML infrastructure
options.C: Automatic retraining of ML models
options.D: Natural language processing capabilities

questions.explanation: AWS Config provides continuous monitoring and recording of AWS resource configurations and their changes over time. For AI governance, this means organizations can track changes to SageMaker endpoints, model configurations, security settings, access controls, and other infrastructure components supporting AI systems. This audit trail helps demonstrate compliance, investigate incidents, and maintain governance over the AI infrastructure.

questions.question: An organization discovers that its customer churn prediction model has developed a significant accuracy disparity between male and female customers after three months in production. What should they use to detect this automatically?

options.A: Amazon SageMaker Autopilot
options.B: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor with bias drift detection configured
options.C: Amazon CloudFront
options.D: Amazon SageMaker Feature Store

questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Model Monitor with bias drift detection can be configured to continuously compute bias metrics on production data and predictions, comparing them against a baseline. When the accuracy disparity between male and female customers exceeds the configured threshold, Model Monitor generates an alert. This automated monitoring ensures fairness degradation is detected promptly without relying on manual periodic reviews.

questions.question: What is 'intersectional bias' in AI systems?

options.A: Bias that only affects a single demographic group
options.B: Bias that emerges at the intersection of multiple protected attributes (e.g., the model is biased specifically against older women, even though it performs fairly for women overall and older people overall)
options.C: Bias caused by the intersection of two different models
options.D: Bias in how different features intersect mathematically

questions.explanation: Intersectional bias occurs when discrimination affects individuals who belong to multiple protected groups simultaneously, even when the model appears fair when each attribute is examined independently. For example, a model might be fair to women as a group and fair to elderly people as a group, but unfair to elderly women specifically. Detecting intersectional bias requires analyzing performance across combinations of protected attributes, not just individual attributes.

questions.question: Under the EU AI Act, what is the classification for AI-powered chatbots that interact with humans?

options.A: Unacceptable risk
options.B: High risk
options.C: Limited risk, with transparency obligations to disclose that users are interacting with an AI
options.D: Minimal risk with no requirements

questions.explanation: Under the EU AI Act, AI systems that interact with natural persons (such as chatbots) are classified as limited risk and are subject to transparency obligations. The primary requirement is that users must be informed that they are interacting with an AI system. AI systems that generate or manipulate content (deepfakes) also fall under limited risk with disclosure requirements. They are not banned (unacceptable risk) or subject to the full compliance regime of high-risk systems.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'federated learning' and its relationship to responsible AI?

options.A: A technique where multiple organizations train the same model by sharing all their data in a central location
options.B: A distributed training approach where models are trained on local data and only model updates (not raw data) are shared, supporting privacy preservation
options.C: A technique for federating access to AI services across AWS accounts
options.D: A method for distributing model predictions across multiple endpoints

questions.explanation: Federated learning is a privacy-preserving machine learning approach where models are trained across multiple decentralized data sources without transferring the raw data to a central location. Instead, each participant trains a local model on their data and only shares model updates (gradients or parameters). These updates are aggregated to improve a global model. This supports the privacy pillar of responsible AI by keeping sensitive data on local devices or within organizational boundaries.

questions.question: A team is developing an AI system and wants to conduct a comprehensive impact assessment before deployment. Which elements should this assessment include?

options.A: Only the model's accuracy on the test set
options.B: Potential benefits and harms, affected stakeholders, fairness evaluation across demographics, privacy risks, safety considerations, mitigation strategies, and ongoing monitoring plans
options.C: Only the cost of deployment
options.D: Only compliance with a single regulation

questions.explanation: A comprehensive AI impact assessment evaluates the full spectrum of potential consequences. This includes identifying potential benefits and harms, mapping all affected stakeholders, evaluating fairness across demographic groups, assessing privacy risks, considering safety implications, developing mitigation strategies for identified risks, and planning for ongoing monitoring. This holistic approach ensures responsible deployment and is increasingly required by AI governance frameworks and regulations.

questions.question: What advantage does Amazon SageMaker Clarify have over building custom bias detection tools?

options.A: It is the only tool that can detect bias in any ML model
options.B: It provides an integrated, managed solution with standardized bias metrics, integration with SageMaker Pipelines and Model Monitor, and documentation that supports compliance and governance
options.C: It guarantees that models will be completely free of bias
options.D: It is free of charge for all AWS customers

questions.explanation: Amazon SageMaker Clarify provides an integrated, managed solution that computes standardized bias metrics recognized in the fairness literature. It integrates with SageMaker Pipelines for automated checks, Model Monitor for continuous monitoring, and SageMaker Studio for visualization. The standardized metrics and generated reports support compliance documentation and governance. While custom tools can also detect bias, SageMaker Clarify reduces development effort and provides a consistent framework.

questions.question: A company uses an AI system to screen job applications. Applicants are not told that AI is involved in the screening process. Which responsible AI principle is violated?

options.A: Robustness
options.B: Privacy
options.C: Transparency
options.D: Fairness

questions.explanation: Transparency requires that individuals be informed when AI is being used to make or support decisions that affect them. Failing to disclose AI involvement in job application screening violates this principle because applicants cannot make informed decisions about the process, cannot contest AI-driven decisions, and are unaware that algorithmic bias could affect their candidacy. Many jurisdictions are also enacting laws requiring disclosure of AI in hiring.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a 'datsheet for datasets' in responsible AI?

options.A: To track the storage costs of datasets
options.B: To provide standardized documentation about dataset composition, collection methodology, intended uses, known biases, ethical considerations, and maintenance plans
options.C: To automatically clean and preprocess the data
options.D: To visualize the dataset in a spreadsheet format

questions.explanation: A 'datasheet for datasets' (proposed by Gebru et al., 2021) is a standardized documentation framework that accompanies datasets used in ML. It includes the dataset's motivation and purpose, composition and demographics, collection process, preprocessing, intended uses and limitations, distribution details, and maintenance plans. Datasheets promote transparency about data provenance and help downstream users understand potential biases and appropriate uses, supporting responsible AI development.

questions.question: A deployed credit scoring model is found to assign systematically lower scores to applicants who list their address in certain neighborhoods. A post-hoc analysis with SageMaker Clarify shows that neighborhood is the most influential feature. What are the responsible next steps?

options.A: No action is needed since the model is using legitimate features
options.B: Investigate whether neighborhood acts as a proxy for protected attributes, assess disparate impact, consider removing or constraining the feature, retrain with fairness constraints, and document the analysis
options.C: Simply remove all address-related features and redeploy without further analysis
options.D: Increase the model's overall accuracy and redeploy

questions.explanation: Neighborhood can be a proxy for race, ethnicity, and socioeconomic status due to historical residential segregation. The responsible approach requires investigating the proxy relationship, quantifying the disparate impact on protected groups, considering whether neighborhood is a legitimate and necessary feature for credit assessment, exploring alternatives such as fairness constraints during training, and thoroughly documenting the analysis and decisions. Simply removing the feature without analysis may not resolve the bias and could reduce model quality unnecessarily.

questions.question: Which of the following represents a tension (trade-off) that responsible AI practitioners commonly face?

options.A: Using AWS services versus using on-premises infrastructure
options.B: Achieving maximum model accuracy versus ensuring fairness across all demographic groups
options.C: Using Python versus Java for model development
options.D: Deploying models in one region versus multiple regions

questions.explanation: One of the most common trade-offs in responsible AI is between maximum predictive accuracy and fairness across demographic groups. Optimizing purely for accuracy may lead to models that perform exceptionally well on average but unfairly for certain groups. Enforcing strict fairness constraints may reduce overall accuracy. Responsible AI practitioners must navigate this trade-off thoughtfully, defining acceptable accuracy-fairness boundaries based on the specific application context, stakeholder needs, and regulatory requirements.

questions.question: An organization has implemented a comprehensive responsible AI program. Which combination of ongoing practices is MOST important for maintaining responsible AI standards over time?

options.A: Continuous monitoring for drift and fairness degradation, periodic re-evaluation of bias metrics, regular stakeholder engagement, updated documentation, and evolving governance policies as regulations change
options.B: Running a one-time bias check at deployment and never revisiting the model
options.C: Only monitoring model accuracy and ignoring fairness metrics
options.D: Relying solely on automated tools without any human oversight

questions.explanation: Responsible AI is not a one-time activity but an ongoing commitment. Maintaining standards requires continuous monitoring (using tools like SageMaker Model Monitor) for data drift, concept drift, and fairness degradation; periodic re-evaluation of bias metrics as real-world conditions change; regular engagement with diverse stakeholders including affected communities; keeping documentation up to date; and evolving governance policies to keep pace with new regulations and best practices. All of these practices together ensure that AI systems remain fair, transparent, and safe throughout their lifecycle.
